bestiary.greece_minotaur.lore: Bull-headed son of Queen Pasiphaë, caged in the Labyrinth that Daedalus built beneath Knossos. It devoured the youths sent as tribute until Theseus followed Ariadne's thread into the dark and slew it.
bestiary.greece_shade.lore: The bloodless soul of the dead, drifting the grey Asphodel Meadows. Odysseus had to pour out offerings of blood before the shades could speak; unfed, they only whisper.
bestiary.greece_skeleton.lore: The Spartoi, the 'sown men' — warriors that sprang fully armed from a dragon's teeth scattered on the earth. They rise to cut down any who trespass on the dead.
bestiary.greece_harpy.lore: A Harpy, one of the winged 'snatchers,' storm-spirits with women's faces. They tormented the blind king Phineus, fouling his food, until the sons of the North Wind drove them away.
bestiary.greece_gorgon.lore: A Gorgon, sister to snake-haired Medusa. To meet her gaze is to turn to cold stone — Perseus struck her using only her reflection in a polished shield.
bestiary.greece_satyr.lore: A goat-legged satyr, wild follower of Dionysus, drunk on wine and revel. Beneath the mirth hides something swift and dangerous when the dance turns to frenzy.
bestiary.greece_hydra_head.lore: A single head of the Lernaean Hydra. Sever one and two more uncoil in its place — only searing fire can close the wound.
bestiary.greece_hydra.lore: The Hydra of Lerna, many-headed venom-beast of the swamp. Heracles' second labor: he prevailed only when Iolaus burned each stump so no new head could grow.
bestiary.greece_cyclops.lore: A Cyclops, one-eyed giant of Etna who forged Zeus's thunderbolts. Their kind was brutal and lawless — Polyphemus, blinded by Odysseus, was one of them.
bestiary.bali_naga.lore: A Naga, serpent-spirit that guards the boundary between the seen and unseen worlds. In Balinese lore the dragon Naga Basuki keeps the balance of the cosmos.
bestiary.bali_leyak.lore: A Leyak — by day an ordinary person, by night a flying head trailing its entrails, feeding on the blood of the sleeping. They serve the witch-queen Rangda.
bestiary.bali_bhuta.lore: A Bhuta-kala, a base spirit of the earth born of the unquiet dead. Offerings are laid at crossroads to appease them and keep the balance of rwa bhineda.
bestiary.bali_celuluk.lore: The Celuluk, a hideous bald hag-spirit and servant of Rangda, sent to frighten children and curse households after dark.
bestiary.bali_garuda.lore: Garuda, the great sun-eagle, mount of Vishnu and eternal foe of the serpent-Nagas — here a lesser kin, radiant and fierce.
bestiary.bali_macan.lore: A Macan, a spectral tiger-spirit of the Balinese wild, swift and silent, sacred and feared in equal measure.
bestiary.bali_rangda.lore: Rangda, the demon-queen of the Leyak, ruler of the unseen. In the eternal barong dance she is chaos incarnate, met and held in balance by the lion-spirit Barong — never truly destroyed.
bestiary.bali_bhuta_lord.lore: A Bhuta-lord, greatest of the earth-demons, gorged on the offerings meant to keep it at bay.
bestiary.egypt_anubis_guard.lore: A jackal-headed guardian of Anubis, god who weighs the heart of the dead against the feather of Ma'at. They watch the scales and guard the embalming halls.
bestiary.egypt_scarab.lore: The scarab, sacred to Khepri who rolls the sun across the sky as a beetle rolls its ball of dung — a sign of rebirth, here swarming and hungry.
bestiary.egypt_shabti.lore: A shabti, a small servant-figure buried with the dead to labor for them in the afterlife. Roused in number, they answer only their master's call.
bestiary.egypt_mummy.lore: An embalmed dead one, bound in linen and preserved so the soul might return to it. Disturb the tomb and it rises to defend its rest.
bestiary.egypt_sandwraith.lore: A restless desert-spirit of the unburied dead, whose name was struck from all memory — to be forgotten is the Egyptian's true death.
bestiary.egypt_serpopard.lore: A serpopard, the long-necked serpent-leopard carved on the oldest palettes of Egypt — a chaos-beast from before the ordered world.
bestiary.egypt_apophis.lore: Apophis (Apep), the great serpent of chaos who each night tries to swallow the sun-boat of Ra. He is fought and repelled eternally, but never slain.
bestiary.egypt_sphinx.lore: The Sphinx, lion-bodied riddler who devoured all who failed her question — until Oedipus answered, and she cast herself from the rock.
bestiary.japan_kitsune.lore: A kitsune, the fox-spirit that grows a new tail with each century of wisdom. It shapeshifts and beguiles — a trickster that can be guardian or menace.
bestiary.japan_onibi.lore: Onibi, 'demon-fire' — pale wisps of the dead that drift over marsh and graveyard, luring the living from the path into the dark.
bestiary.japan_kappa.lore: A kappa, river-imp with a water-filled dish on its head. Drain the dish and it loses its power; it is fond of cucumbers and of drowning the careless.
bestiary.japan_oni.lore: An oni, horned ogre of the Buddhist hells who torments the wicked. Clubs in hand, they are the brutish wardens of the underworld.
bestiary.japan_yurei.lore: A yūrei, a vengeful ghost held to the world by grief or rage, unable to pass on until its wrong is set right.
bestiary.japan_tsuchigumo.lore: The tsuchigumo, the monstrous 'earth-spider' that ensnared the hero Yorimitsu in its web before he cut it open.
bestiary.japan_orochi.lore: Yamata-no-Orochi, the eight-headed, eight-tailed serpent that demanded a maiden each year — slain by the storm-god Susanoo, who made it drunk on eight vats of sake.
bestiary.japan_tengu.lore: A tengu, long-nosed winged spirit of the mountains, master of the sword and of trickery, both trainer of heroes and punisher of the proud.
bestiary.norse_ulfhednar.lore: An úlfheðinn, 'wolf-coat' — a warrior of Odin who fought in a battle-frenzy wearing the skin of a wolf, kin to the berserkers.
bestiary.norse_helhound.lore: A hound of Hel, kin to Garmr who guards the gates of the death-realm and will break loose to howl at Ragnarök.
bestiary.norse_draugr.lore: A draugr, the undead of the burial mound, swollen and death-blue, jealously guarding its grave-hoard with corpse-strength.
bestiary.norse_jotunn.lore: A jötunn, a giant of frost and stone, ancient enemy of the gods of Asgard from the first days of the world.
bestiary.norse_frost_archer.lore: A frost-giant's bowman from Niflheim, loosing shards of killing ice across the cold wastes.
bestiary.norse_vargr.lore: A vargr, a great wolf of the wild — kin to Fenrir's brood Sköll and Hati, who chase the sun and moon across the sky.
bestiary.norse_fenrir.lore: Fenrir, the monstrous wolf whose jaws stretch from earth to sky. The gods bound him with the impossible ribbon Gleipnir at the cost of Týr's hand; at Ragnarök he breaks free and devours Odin.
bestiary.norse_troll.lore: A troll of the mountains, slow and mighty, turned to stone if the sun should catch it above ground.
bestiary.aztec_eagle_warrior.lore: An eagle warrior, elite soldier of the sun-god Huitzilopochtli, who took captives so their hearts might feed the sun and keep it rising.
bestiary.aztec_obsidian.lore: A spirit of itztli, sacred obsidian — the black volcanic glass of sacrificial blades, edged sharper than any steel.
bestiary.aztec_jaguar.lore: A jaguar-spirit of Tezcatlipoca, 'Smoking Mirror,' lord of night and sorcery who prowls the world in the great cat's shape.
bestiary.aztec_tzitzimitl.lore: A tzitzimitl, a skeletal star-demon that hangs in the sky by day and, at eclipse, falls to devour humankind.
bestiary.aztec_atlatl.lore: A warrior armed with the atlatl, the spear-thrower that hurls darts with killing force across the field.
bestiary.aztec_xolotl.lore: Xolotl, the dog-headed twin of Quetzalcoatl who guides the dead through Mictlan's nine layers to their final rest.
bestiary.aztec_cipactli.lore: Cipactli, the primeval crocodile-monster of chaos. The gods tore her body apart to make the earth and sky — hungry at every joint, she demanded blood in return.
bestiary.aztec_jaguar_lord.lore: The Jaguar Lord, greatest of Tezcatlipoca's night-cats, a shadow with teeth prowling the edge of the fires.
bestiary.hell_spawn.lore: A star-spawn of Cthulhu, lesser kin to the Great Old One, spilled through from the sunken city of R'lyeh where the dead god waits dreaming.
bestiary.hell_byakhee.lore: A byakhee, a winged interstellar thing that rides the void between stars, summoned by those who call the wrong names beneath the wrong stars.
bestiary.hell_deep_one.lore: A Deep One, immortal fish-frog dweller of the drowned deeps who breeds with coastal folk and worships Dagon and Hydra.
bestiary.hell_shoggoth.lore: A shoggoth, a vast protoplasmic slave-thing shaped by the Elder Things — a boiling mass of eyes that learned, at last, to turn on its makers.
bestiary.hell_mi_go.lore: A Mi-go, the 'fungus from Yuggoth,' a crustacean-winged alien that mines distant worlds and carries human minds away in cylinders.
bestiary.hell_cultist.lore: A robed cultist of the Old Ones, who keeps the death-cult alive across the ages, chanting for the day the stars come right and the dreamer wakes.
bestiary.hell_dagon.lore: Dagon, the vast Deep One patriarch worshipped as a god by the drowned — a titan risen from the black trenches of the sea.
bestiary.hell_cthulhu.lore: Great Cthulhu, the dead-but-dreaming priest of the Old Ones, entombed in sunken R'lyeh. When the stars align his city will rise and he will wake — and the world will end in ecstasy and ruin.
